mainTopic: How serious it is to shame or hurt people with words (אונאת דברים), especially one's wife, plus teachings on household peace and the opening of the oven of עכנאי.
overview: This amud continues the theme of אונאת דברים, hurting people with words. It opens with two powerful teachings: it is better to sin with a possible אשת איש than to shame someone in public, learned from דוד's words, and better to be thrown into a fiery furnace, learned from תמר. Then come teachings about hurting people: who counts as 'your fellow,' and רב's warning to be careful not to hurt one's wife, since her tears come easily. רבי אלעזר teaches that the gates of tears are never locked. רב warns against following a wife's advice, and the גמרא limits this to certain kinds of matters. Next, רב חסדא, רבי אלעזר and רבי אבהו show that ה׳ hears the cry of someone hurt by אונאה and punishes it Himself. A series of 'always be careful' teachings follows: keep grain at home for peace and against poverty, and honor your wife, since blessing comes through her. The amud ends by quoting a משנה about an oven cut into rings, which opens the famous story of תנור של עכנאי on the next amud.

steps.title: Better a doubtful sin than public embarrassment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that it is better to have relations with a woman who might be an אשת איש than to embarrass someone in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is better for a person to have relations with a woman who may be married than to embarrass his friend in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a very strong statement about how serious it is to shame someone in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with an אשת איש is one of the worst sins in the תורה. Saying it is 'better' than public embarrassment shows how terrible הלבנת פנים is. The case uses a ספק, a doubtful married woman, so it is not a case of a definite אשת איש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is better for a person
A woman who may or may not be married

phrases.english: It is better for a person
to have relations with a woman who may be married,
and not embarrass his friend in public.
phrases.notes: Literally 'whiten his friend's face.' When someone is shamed, the color drains from their face.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹחַ לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁיָּבוֹא עַל סְפֵק אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Public embarrassment is worse than relations with a possible אשת איש.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn this.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the strong statement it just made. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an extreme claim needs proof. The answer will come from a דרשה of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא לַן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the idea that public embarrassment is worse than a doubtful אשת איש.

steps.title: רבא's reading of דוד's words
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains a פסוק in תהלים as דוד telling הקדוש ברוך הוא how much he had suffered, so that even if his flesh were torn, no blood would come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what רבא taught about the פסוק 'when I limped they rejoiced... they tore and did not stop.' דוד said to הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the World, You know that if they tore my flesh, my blood would not drip to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with רבא's explanation of a פסוק in which דוד describes his suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the word דמו as related to דם, blood. דוד is saying he had weakened himself so much that his flesh had no blood left in it. This sets the scene for the real proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: From what Rava taught,
for Rava taught:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And when I limped they rejoiced and gathered...
phrases.notes: תהלים 35:15

phrases.english: they tore and did not stop"?
phrases.notes: דמו sounds like דם, blood, and רבא builds on that.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
it is revealed and known before You
that if they were to tear my flesh,
my blood would not drip onto the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּדָרֵשׁ רָבָא, דְּדָרֵשׁ רָבָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is רבא's דרשה on תהלים 35:15 about דוד's suffering.

steps.title: דוד: the one who shames has no share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: People mocked דוד by asking him the punishment for an אשת איש. He answered that such a sinner still has a share in עולם הבא, but one who shames others in public does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: even while they are learning the laws of נגעים and אהלות, they say to me, 'דוד, what is the death penalty for one who has relations with an אשת איש?' I tell them: 'He dies by חנק, but he has a share in עולם הבא. But one who embarrasses his friend in public has no share in עולם הבא.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual proof: דוד himself says that public shaming is worse than the sin of אשת איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an אשת איש sinner who is put to death keeps his share in עולם הבא. One who shames others in public loses it completely. That is why it is 'better' to do the first sin than the second.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even more
Laws of impurity spread by a dead body under a roof
Death by choking, one of the four court death penalties
A share in the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: Public shaming is worse than a capital sin: the one who shames loses his share in עולם הבא, while the אשת איש sinner does not.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean one may actually sin with an אשת איש to avoid embarrassing someone. The point is to show how severe public shaming is.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
even at the time when they are busy learning
the laws of skin-afflictions and tents,
phrases.notes: These topics have nothing to do with his sin. They bring it up anyway, just to shame him.

phrases.english: they say to me: "David,
one who has relations with a married woman,
what is his death penalty?"
And I say to them:
"His death is by strangling,
and he has a share in the World to Come.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַמַּלְבִּין אֶת פְּנֵי חֲבֵירוֹ בָּרַבִּים,
phrases.english: But one who embarrasses his friend in public
has no share in the World to Come."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא, אֲפִילּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעוֹסְקִין בִּנְגָעִים וְאֹהָלוֹת
steps.raayaObject: The statement in step 1 that public shaming is worse than a possible אשת איש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דוד's words in רבא's דרשה: the אשת איש sinner keeps his share in עולם הבא, but one who shames others loses it.

steps.title: Better a fiery furnace than shaming someone
steps.stepSummary: A teaching handed down in several versions of who said it: it is better to throw yourself into a fiery furnace than to embarrass someone in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב (some say רב חנא בר ביזנא in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא, and some say רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי): It is better for a person to throw himself into a fiery furnace than to embarrass his friend in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second strong teaching about public embarrassment and gives three versions of who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than step 1. Here a person should give up his own life rather than shame someone in public. The three names are simply different traditions of who taught it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: And Mar Zutra bar Toviya said in the name of Rav,
and some say:
Rav Chana bar Bizna said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon Chasida,
and some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is better for a person
to throw himself into a fiery furnace
and not embarrass his friend in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹחַ לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּפִּיל עַצְמוֹ לְכִבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should rather be thrown into a fiery furnace than embarrass someone in public.

steps.title: Asking for the source again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the furnace teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the furnace teaching. This sets up the answer from תמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up your life is a huge demand, so the גמרא wants a clear source from the תורה.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא לַן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for giving up one's life rather than shaming someone in public.

steps.title: The proof from תמר
steps.stepSummary: The source is תמר. As she was being taken out to be burned, she sent a hint to יהודה instead of shaming him in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: From תמר, as it is written: 'She was being taken out, and she sent to her father-in-law.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the story of תמר and יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמר was being taken out to be burned. She did not announce that יהודה was the father. Instead, she quietly sent him his belongings, leaving it to him to admit it. She was ready to be burned rather than shame him publicly.
steps.whatToRemember: תמר chose to risk being burned rather than publicly shame יהודה. That is the source for 'better a fiery furnace than public embarrassment.'

phrases.english: From Tamar,
as it is written:
"She was being taken out
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:25

phrases.english: and she sent to her father-in-law."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתָּמָר, דִּכְתִיב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמר sent a private message to יהודה even while being taken out to be burned, rather than shaming him.

steps.title: Do not hurt a fellow in תורה and מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב חננא בריה דרב אידי reads the word עמיתו as 'the people who are with you' in תורה and מצוות. Those people you must not hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חננא son of רב אידי said: What does the פסוק 'You shall not hurt each man his fellow (עמיתו)' mean? A people that is with you in תורה and מצוות, do not hurt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a דרשה on the main פסוק of אונאת דברים, explaining who 'your fellow' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits עמיתו into עם אתו, 'the people with him.' The prohibition is focused on a fellow Jew who shares a life of תורה and מצוות with you.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִנָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Chinana son of Rav Idi said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And you shall not hurt each man his fellow"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:17

phrases.english: A people that is with you in Torah and מצוות,
phrases.notes: He reads עמיתו as עם אתו, 'the people who are with him.'

phrases.english: do not hurt him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִנָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמיתו means one who is with you in תורה and מצוות. Such a person must not be hurt.

steps.title: Be careful not to hurt your wife
steps.stepSummary: רב warns that a man must always be careful not to hurt his wife's feelings. Because she cries easily, the punishment for hurting her comes quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A person should always be careful not to hurt his wife's feelings. Since her tears come easily, the punishment for hurting her is close.
steps.whatsHappening: רב applies אונאת דברים to the home and gives a special warning about one's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her pain shows up quickly in tears, and tears bring a quick response from Heaven. So hurting her brings punishment fast.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that אונאת דברים is not only about strangers or business. It applies most of all to the people closest to us.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A person should always be careful
about hurting his wife's feelings,
because since her tears come easily,
the punishment for hurting her comes quickly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם זָהִיר בְּאוֹנָאַת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man must always be careful not to hurt his wife, because punishment for hurting her comes quickly.

steps.title: The gates of prayer are locked, but the gates of tears are open
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that since the חורבן, prayer is not accepted the way it once was, but prayer with tears is still heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the gates of prayer were locked, as it says: 'Even when I cry out and plead, He shuts out my prayer.' But even though the gates of prayer were locked, the gates of tears were not locked, as it says: 'Hear my prayer, ה׳, and listen to my pleading; do not be silent to my tears.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains that since the בית המקדש was destroyed, ordinary prayer has a harder time getting through, but tears still go straight up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He brings two פסוקים: one shows prayer being 'shut out', and the other shows דוד asking ה׳ not to stay silent at his tears. This explains the end of step 9: a wife who is hurt cries easily, and tears always reach ה׳, so the punishment comes quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: The gates of prayer, meaning the way prayer goes up to ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the reason behind רב's warning in step 9: the tears of someone who was hurt are never blocked.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
the gates of prayer were locked,
as it says: "Even when I cry out and plead,
He shuts out my prayer."
phrases.notes: איכה 3:8

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשַּׁעֲרֵי תְפִילָּה נִנְעֲלוּ,
phrases.english: And even though the gates of prayer were locked,
the gates of tears were not locked,
as it says: "Hear my prayer, ה׳,
and listen to my pleading,
do not be silent to my tears."
phrases.notes: תהלים 39:13

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִיּוֹם שֶׁנֶּחְרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the tears of a hurt wife (step 9) bring quick punishment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן prayer is blocked, but tears are always heard.

steps.title: Following a wife's advice can lead to גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a man who follows his wife's advice falls into גיהנם, learning it from אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: Anyone who follows his wife's advice falls into גיהנם, as it says: 'But there was none like אחאב,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds another teaching about husbands and wives: a man who simply follows his wife's advice can end up in גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is אחאב, whose wife איזבל pushed him to do evil. Next, רב פפא challenges this rule from a popular saying that tells a man to consult his wife, and the גמרא will limit the rule to certain kinds of matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of punishment after death

phrases.english: And Rav said:
Anyone who follows his wife's advice
falls into Gehinnom,
as it says: "But there was none like Achav, etc."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 21:25. The rest of the פסוק says his wife איזבל pushed him to do evil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַהוֹלֵךְ בַּעֲצַת אִשְׁתּוֹ נוֹפֵל בְּגֵיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רב about a man and his wife, this time giving the other side
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following a wife's advice blindly can lead to גיהנם, as with אחאב.

steps.title: A popular saying tells you to ask your wife
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רב's rule from a common saying that tells a man to go out of his way to ask his wife's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But don't people say, 'If your wife is short, bend down and whisper to her'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks אביי a question: a well-known saying tells a husband to ask his wife's opinion, which seems to clash with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying means that even if it takes effort (bending down to a short wife), you should consult her. So how can רב say that following her advice leads to גיהנם?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But don't people say,
"If your wife is short,
bend down and whisper to her!"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that following a wife's advice leads to גיהנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A common saying tells a man to consult his wife, which seems to contradict רב.

steps.title: First answer: worldly matters versus household matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב means general worldly matters, and the saying means household matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is about general worldly matters, and that is about household matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two statements are about different kinds of decisions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's warning is about general worldly matters, and there a man should not just follow his wife. The saying is about running the home, and there he should ask her.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no contradiction

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about general worldly matters,
phrases.notes: "This" means רב's rule not to follow her advice.

phrases.english: and that is about household matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּמִילֵּי דְעָלְמָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different areas of life)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the saying seem to contradict each other about consulting a wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: Don't simply follow her in general worldly matters; do consult her in household matters.

steps.title: Second version: matters of Heaven versus worldly matters
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the answer: רב means religious matters, and the saying means general worldly matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: this is about matters of Heaven, and that is about general worldly matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same answer, drawing the line in a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב's warning is limited to matters of Heaven, the kind of thing אחאב was led astray in. In everyday worldly matters a man should consult his wife. So in this version, worldly matters move to the side where her advice is welcome.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch: in the first version worldly matters are where you should NOT follow her, but in this version worldly matters are where you SHOULD consult her.

phrases.english: Another version:
this is about matters of Heaven,
and that is about general worldly matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative wording of the answer in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (a different dividing line)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first answer put worldly matters on רב's side.
steps.terutzMaskana: Don't follow her in matters of Heaven; do consult her in worldly matters.

steps.title: The gates for hurtful words are never locked
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that all gates may be locked except the gates for someone hurt by אונאה, learned from the plumb line in ה׳'s hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: All the gates are locked except for the gates of hurtful words, as it says: 'Behold, ה׳ stands on a wall made with a plumb line, and a plumb line in His hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main theme of hurting people: רב חסדא says the cry of someone hurt by אונאה is never blocked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי אלעזר's 'gates of tears' in step 10, there is another gate that always stays open: the gate of אונאה. The proof is the word אֲנָךְ, which sounds like אונאה, held in ה׳'s own hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Hurting or wronging someone, here mainly with words
A plumb line, a builder's measuring weight

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
All the gates are locked,
except for the gates of hurtful words,
as it says: "Behold, ה׳ stands
on a wall made with a plumb line, and a plumb line in His hand."
phrases.notes: עמוס 7:7. The word אֲנָךְ looks and sounds like אונאה, so the גמרא reads it as a hint to hurting people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: כׇּל הַשְּׁעָרִים נִנְעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of open gates from step 10, now about אונאה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cry of someone hurt by אונאה is never blocked.

steps.title: ה׳ punishes hurtful words Himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that every sin is punished through a messenger, except אונאה, which ה׳ punishes Himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Everything is punished through a messenger, except for hurtful words, as it says: 'and a plumb line in His hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר uses the same פסוק to add something new: ה׳ handles the punishment for אונאה personally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually ה׳ punishes through some agent. But the פסוק says the אֲנָךְ is 'in His hand', so for אונאה the punishment comes straight from ה׳.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Everything is punished through a messenger,
except for hurtful words,
as it says: "and a plumb line in His hand."
phrases.notes: "In His hand" means ה׳ Himself, not a messenger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַכֹּל נִפְרָע בִּידֵי שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching drawn from the same פסוק as step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ Himself punishes אונאה, not a messenger.

steps.title: Three sins that reach straight to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that the curtain before ה׳ is never closed to three sins: אונאה, גזל and עבודה זרה, each with its own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: There are three things before which the curtain is not locked: hurtful words, robbery, and idol worship. Hurtful words, as it is written: 'and a plumb line in His hand.' Robbery, as it is written: 'Violence and robbery are heard in her, before Me always.' Idol worship, as it is written: 'The people who anger Me before Me always,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו lists three sins that go straight up to ה׳ with nothing blocking them, and gives a פסוק for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אונאה again comes from 'in His hand.' For גזל and עבודה זרה, both פסוקים use the words 'before Me always', showing these sins stand right in front of ה׳. So אונאה is placed in the same group as robbery and idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain between this world and the שכינה

steps.whatToRemember: Hurting someone, especially with words, is extremely serious. The victim's tears and cries are never blocked, ה׳ punishes it Himself, and it reaches Him directly, together with גזל and עבודה זרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the section by showing how seriously the תורה views אונאה, the theme of this whole part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
There are three things before which the curtain is not locked:
phrases.notes: The פרגוד is the curtain between this world and the שכינה.

phrases.english: hurtful words, robbery, and idol worship.
Hurtful words, as it is written: "and a plumb line in His hand."
Robbery, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״חָמָס וָשֹׁד יִשָּׁמַע בָּהּ עַל פָּנַי תָּמִיד״.
phrases.english: "Violence and robbery are heard in her, before Me always."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 6:7

phrases.english: Idol worship, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״הָעָם הַמַּכְעִיסִים אוֹתִי עַל פָּנַי תָּמִיד וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "The people who anger Me before Me always, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 65:3

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵין הַפַּרְגּוֹד נִנְעָל בִּפְנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the teaching about אונאה into a list of three sins that reach ה׳ directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אונאה, גזל and עבודה זרה reach ה׳ with no barrier.

steps.title: Keep grain in the house to keep peace
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that a person must make sure there is grain at home, because household fights come mostly from shortages of food. He brings a פסוק from תהלים that links peace with wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A person should always be careful to have grain in his house. Arguments in a home usually come only over grain, as the פסוק says: 'He makes your borders peace; He fills you with the finest wheat.'
steps.whatsHappening: Following the earlier teachings about how to treat people at home, the גמרא brings a new practical teaching from רב יהודה about keeping food in the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a lack of basic food creates tension in a home. The פסוק puts 'peace' right next to 'finest wheat,' showing that having enough food helps bring peace.

keyTerms.meaning: A person should always be careful (a standard opening for advice)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A person should always be careful
about grain inside his house,
for arguing is not found
in a person's house
except over matters of grain,
as it says: "He makes your borders peace;
phrases.notes: תהלים 147:14

phrases.english: He satisfies you with the finest wheat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם זָהִיר בִּתְבוּאָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of household and conduct teachings with a new statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Make sure there is grain at home, because a lack of food is the main cause of household quarrels.

steps.title: A folk saying backs up the grain teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that a common saying matches רב יהודה's teaching: when the barley runs out, fighting comes into the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: When the barley is gone from the jug, a quarrel comes knocking and enters the house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא supports רב יהודה's teaching by quoting a popular saying that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule. The everyday saying simply shows that people already know from experience that an empty pantry leads to fights.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what people say:
When the barley is used up from the jug,
a quarrel knocks and comes into the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18 with a popular saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The folk saying confirms that running out of food brings fighting into the home.

steps.title: Israel was called poor only over grain
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר פפא also teaches that one must make sure there is grain at home. He proves from פסוקים in שופטים that the Jewish people were called 'poor' because מדין destroyed their crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר פפא said: A person should always be careful to have grain in his house, because the Jewish people were called poor only over grain. It says: 'And it was, when Israel sowed...', and: 'They camped against them...', and: 'Israel became very poor because of מדין.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives the same advice about grain, but for a different reason: lacking grain is what counts as real poverty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said missing grain causes fighting. רב חיננא בר פפא adds that missing grain is what makes a person poor. The פסוקים show the order of events: Israel planted, מדין came and ruined the crops, and only then is Israel called 'very poor.'

keyTerms.meaning: Midian, the nation that attacked Israel

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa said:
A person should always be careful
about grain inside his house,
for the Jewish people were not called poor
except over matters of grain,
as it says: "And it was, when Israel sowed, etc."
phrases.notes: שופטים 6:3. The rest of the פסוק says מדין came up against them.

phrases.english: and it is written: "And they camped against them, etc."
phrases.notes: שופטים 6:4. It goes on to say they destroyed the crops.

phrases.english: and it is written: "And Israel became very poor because of Midian."
phrases.notes: שופטים 6:6

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם זָהִיר בִּתְבוּאָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel teaching to step 18 with the same advice and a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lacking grain is what defines poverty, as shown when מדין destroyed Israel's crops.

steps.title: Honor your wife, because blessing comes through her
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו teaches that a man must be careful to honor his wife, because the blessing in his home comes because of her. He proves it from אברם, who was treated well because of שרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: A person should always be careful about his wife's honor, because blessing is found in a person's home only because of his wife, as it says: 'And he treated אברם well for her sake.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third teaching in the same style, this time about honoring one's wife instead of keeping grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from food to the wife's dignity. The proof is the story in בראשית: פרעה gave אברם wealth because of שרה, which shows that a household's blessing comes through the wife.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥelbo said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם זָהִיר בִּכְבוֹד אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should always be careful about his wife's honor,
for blessing is not found
in a person's house
except because of his wife,
as it says: "And he treated Abram well for her sake."
phrases.notes: בראשית 12:16. 'He' is פרעה and 'her' is שרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם זָהִיר בִּכְבוֹד אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same 'always be careful' series, now about one's wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honor your wife, because the blessing of the home comes through her.

steps.title: רבא tells the people of מחוזא to honor their wives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects רבי חלבו's teaching to רבא's advice to the people of מחוזא: honor your wives so that you become rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבא told the people of מחוזא: Honor your wives, so that you will become wealthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's practical advice to his community follows the same idea as רבי חלבו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חלבו spoke of 'blessing' in general terms. רבא makes it concrete: honoring your wife leads to wealth. This also closes the series of household teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what (he) said, linking to an earlier idea

steps.whatToRemember: Three 'always be careful' teachings: keep grain at home to keep peace (רב יהודה), keep grain at home to avoid poverty (רב חיננא בר פפא), and honor your wife because blessing comes through her (רבי חלבו, backed up by רבא).

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לִבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא:
phrases.english: And this is what Rava said to the people of Meḥoza:
Honor your wives,
so that you will become rich.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לִבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 21 with רבא's practical advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honor your wives so that you will prosper.

steps.title: The משנה about an oven cut into rings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת כלים: an oven was cut into rings with sand placed between them. רבי אליעזר says it is טהור, and the חכמים say it is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: If someone cut an oven into rings and put sand between each ring, רבי אליעזר says it is pure, and the חכמים say it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes topic and quotes a משנה about a cut-up oven. This sets up the famous story that comes next, which connects back to hurting people with words (אונאת דברים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether an oven made of separate rings counts as a complete כלי. רבי אליעזר says the rings and sand mean it is not a whole כלי, so it cannot become טמא. The חכמים say it still works as an oven, so it can become טמא. This מחלוקת is the background for the story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, in a משנה elsewhere

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new subject that drops the topic of אונאה. The גמרא brings this משנה because the story built on it shows how hurtful words can be.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the famous story of the oven (תנור של עכנאי), one of the best-known passages in the whole ש״ס.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מסכת כלים (5:10).

phrases.english: If one cut it into rings,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a clay oven, which the משנה is discussing.

phrases.english: and put sand between one ring and the next —
Rabbi Eliezer rules it pure,
and the Rabbis rule it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: חֲתָכוֹ חוּלְיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section tied to the earlier theme of אונאת דברים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an oven cut into rings with sand between them, רבי אליעזר rules it טהור and the חכמים rule it טמא.
